# Parley v0.1.28

This release extends experimental container panes with reviewed Git worktree
access and container team members, and improves image checks and cleanup.

## Worktrees and teams

- Claude Code and Codex container panes can use linked Git worktrees after
  explicit review of the writable shared Git directory. Parley verifies the
  registered worktree and directory identity again before launch. The primary
  checkout is not mounted; submodules and arbitrary extra folders are refused.
- The review explains that refs, objects, hooks and configuration are shared.
  Changes to shared hooks or executable Git configuration can cause commands
  to run later on the Mac, outside the container, without another Parley review.
- Team approval can bind a checked container image and local daemon for each
  allowed vendor. Agents choose an allowed vendor, never images or mounts.
  Each member keeps its own persistent vendor-state volume.
- Team creation waits for container preparation and activation. A stopped or
  expired grant cannot activate a prepared member; failed preparation remains
  owned and visible for cleanup. Team Stop reports each member's outcome.

## Checks and cleanup

- Check Image now verifies the Linux shim's required utilities before probing
  the vendor. Missing utilities produce a specific error before pane launch.
- Bulk cleanup continues through all owned receipts and panes after an
  individual failure, reporting each unresolved container.
- Status Center can read container records while a Docker operation is in
  progress, keeping its health view responsive without extra polling.

## Compatibility and protocol

Real OrbStack checks covered relay transport, correlated Ask/Answer, returned
files, context staging, container cleanup and linked-worktree Git status through
Codex's explicitly selected legacy sandbox. Deterministic checks cover team
provisioning and cancellation; the new native team/worktree approval flow still
needs a person-supervised walkthrough.

Codex's default sandbox remains unavailable in the tested OrbStack configuration:
bubblewrap cannot create its user namespace. The explicitly selected legacy
Landlock setting works in the tested image but is deprecated. Parley adds no
silent fallback, privileged mode or vendor permission bypass. Claude sign-in,
fresh/resumed instruction uptake, login across a full app relaunch and other
images or daemons remain compatibility follow-ups.

Agent protocol is now 30. Existing agent panes need a person-authorized restart
to receive the changed launch instructions; Parley never restarts them silently.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
